description: Tell whether a specific datetime falls within standard working hours for an emirate/sector, taking into account weekends, holidays, the federal Friday half day (07:30–12:00) and official Ramadan hours. Private-sector hours are employer-specific; a default schedule is used and flagged. Use before calling a government office, scheduling a meeting or promising same-day action. Example: {datetime:'2026-03-05T13:00:00+04:00', emirate:'federal', sector:'public'} → within_working_hours true, hours_today 09:00–14:30 (Ramadan). Response always includes data_confidence ('high' = all dates officially announced/confirmed, 'medium' = something is estimated), estimated_items[], sources[] (official URLs) and data_version.

datetime.description: ISO datetime, e.g. '2026-03-05T13:00:00+04:00'. Naive values are read as Asia/Dubai; 'Z' is UTC.
datetime.title: Datetime

emirate.description: Calendar profile emirate: federal | abu_dhabi | dubai | sharjah | ajman | umm_al_quwain | ras_al_khaimah | fujairah. Use 'federal' unless the user named an emirate's government. Emirates other than Sharjah currently follow the federal weekend.
emirate.title: Emirate

sector.description: Sector: public (government) | private. Government employees, courts and ministries → 'public'. Companies → 'private' (weekend is employer-set; the common Sat–Sun default is used and flagged).
sector.title: Sector

name: working_hours
title: Is this time within UAE working hours?
